findings.explanation: Deetjen's private NPV is energy cost savings minus the amortized installation cost (deetjen L228-L233); in a video about running cost, 'leaves the homeowner with a private economic loss' will be heard as the heat pump costing more to run than oil, which the passage does not establish.
findings.suggestion: Say the loss is counted once the cost of buying and installing the heat pump is included, e.g. 'usually leaves the homeowner worse off once the installation cost is counted'.

findings.explanation: The same Wilson passage (L401-L406, inside s10's cited range) says most homes with higher bills are hot-climate homes without AC where new cooling costs outweigh heating savings; without that, a viewer hears that the heat pump lost on heating in up to a quarter of these homes.

findings.explanation: s16's note drops Deetjen's oil result because its NPV counts installation cost, yet s20 keeps RMI's oil result, which is the same kind of measure: L817-L820 sit under 'RESULTS: PROVIDENCE, RI' and Figure 18, the 15-year net present cost of water and space conditioning, equipment included (L800-L816 compare retrofit costs). Keeping the capital-inclusive result that favours the heat pump and dropping the one that goes against it, in a running-cost video, tilts the oil verdict; 'net present cost' will be heard as cheaper to run.
findings.suggestion: Treat both alike: either cut RMI's net-present-cost result (s19-s20, re-introducing the analysis in s21) so the oil section rests on running-cost evidence, or report both capital-inclusive results side by side with the measure named in words a cited passage supports.
